items.snippet: 이재명 대통령의 국정 지지율이 긍정 평가 39%, 부정 평가 50%로 집계됐다. 한국갤럽이 10∼12일 전국 만 18세 이상 1002명을 대상으로 실시해 13일 발표한 여론조사(전화면접 방식, 95% 신뢰수준에 표본오차 ±3.1%포인트, 자세한 사항은 중앙선거여론조사심의위원회 홈페이지 참조)에서 이 대통령의 국정에 대한 평가는 이같이 나타났다. 지난주 조사에서는 긍정 평가 41%, 부정 평가 50%였다. 긍정 평가 이유는 ‘경제·민생’(19%), ‘외교’(17%), ‘소통’(9%), 부정 평가 이유는 ‘부동산 정책’(17%), ‘경제·민생’(15%), ‘도덕성 문제·본인 재판 회피’(12%) 순이었다. 정당 지지율은 민주당 39%, 국민의힘 26%로 집계됐다. 지난주 조사에서는 민주당 36%, 국민의힘 28%였다. 양당 격차는 9월 추석 이후...

items.title: “아는 게 없다” 때리더니… 인천공항 사장 또 낙하산

items.title: 신고할 땐 안 주고… 숨진 다음날 유족에 스마트워치 준 경찰
items.snippet: 지난 10일 살해된 A(15)양의 가족에게 경찰은 사건 발생 이튿날 긴급 신고용 스마트워치 3대를 지급했다. A양을 살해한 진모(59)씨 등 가해자 측이 유족을 위협할 우려가 있다는 이유였다. 그러나 A양 아버지는 본지에 “정작 스마트워치가 필요했던 건 내가 아니라 딸이었다”며 “딸이 살아 있을 때 수차례 실종 신고를 해도 주지 않더니 이제 와서 무슨 소용이냐”고 했다. 그는 “경찰은 꼭 일이 터지고 나서야 뭔가를 하는 것 같다”고 했다.

items.title: “스마트안경 못 잡은거 아니야?” 다른 자격시험까지 번진 불신
items.snippet: 올해 세무사 자격 시험 수석 합격자가 인공지능(AI) 스마트 안경을 이용해 부정행위를 한 것 아니냐는 의혹이 불거진 데 이어 다른 전문 자격 시험에서도 부정이 있었던 것 아니냐는 의혹이 제기됐다. 아직 세무사 시험 수석 합격자가 부정행위를 했다는 증거는 발견되지 않았다. 그런데도 일부 수험생은 ‘스마트 안경 도움 없이는 나올 수 없는 점수가 다른 시험에서도 나왔다’며 의구심을 제기하고 있다. 논란이 커지자 세무사 시험 수석 합격자 A(34)씨는 법률 대리인을 통해 “이번 일에 관한 사실관계 확인을 위해 필요한 절차에 성실히 임할 것”이라고 13일 밝혔다.

items.title: ‘남대문 스카프 아저씨’ 보조 알바 해보니… 아이돌급 환호에 이유 있었다
items.snippet: 그저 ‘남대문 스카프 아저씨(이하 아저씨)’와 몇 마디 나눠 볼 요량이었다. 평범한 시장 상인이 하루아침에 스타가 된 이유가 궁금했다. 그의 스카프 매장에서 일일 알바를 하게 될 줄은 몰랐다. 발단은 이렇다. 9일 오전 9시 50분쯤, 그가 일하는 서울 중구 남대문시장 ‘한양사’ 앞에는 손님 수십여 명이 줄을 서 있었다. 나도 그 틈에 끼어 있었다. 매장 오픈 전이었다.

items.title: 시키지도 않은 일까지 척척… 이 비서, 믿어도 될까
items.snippet: 최근 직장인 김모(44)씨는 스마트폰 화면을 보다가 가슴이 철렁 내려앉았다. 시키지도 않았는데 인공지능(AI) 비서가 직장 근처 식당 여러 곳에 전화를 건 것이다. 당황한 김씨가 이유를 묻자 “회식 장소를 추천해 달라고 하기에 예약이 가능한지 확인한 것”이라는 답이 돌아왔다. 질문에 답하는 데 그치지 않고 예약·결제 등 실제 업무까지 대신 처리하는 ‘AI 에이전트’가 국내에서도 확산하고 있다. 특히 한국어 맥락과 국내 생활 환경에 특화된 에이전트 서비스들이 출시되면서, 이른바 ‘IT 문외한’들도 손쉽게 AI 비서를 부리는 시대가 열렸다. 하지만 편리함만큼 우려도 작지 않다. 사람의 의도를 잘못 이해하거나, 지시하지 않은 일을 제멋대로 처리하는 일이 벌어지고 있기 때문이다.

items.title: 1500년 전 백제의 화려한 금빛 무늬
items.snippet: 예전에 국립공주박물관이 개최한 무령왕릉 발굴 50주년 기념 특별전을 보러 간 적이 있다. 전시 준비와 운영 업무로 담당 학예사는 피곤한 기색이 역력했지만, 어느 것 하나 허투루 볼 수 없는 알찬 유물들로 이루어진 전시를 보며 그를 부러워했던 기억이 있다. 유물에 귀천이 있는 것은 아니며, 미처 주목받지 못한 유물의 의미를 밝히는 것은 무척이나 보람된 일이다. 그러나 무령왕릉 출토품 수준의 유물을, 게다가 그 일괄을 가까이에서 보고 다루는 기회는 특별하다. 마치 김연아 선수의 최고 연기를 본 후에 다른 피겨스케이팅 선수의 실력을 한층 쉽게 가늠할 수 있는 것처럼, 이러한 경험 후에는 유물을 보는 안목과 시야가 달라지기 때문이다.

items.title: 서양 사람은 정말 술안주 안 먹나
items.snippet: “서양 사람들은 술 마실 때 안주를 안 먹나요?” 술 강의를 나가면 거의 빠지지 않고 받는 질문이다. 영화나 드라마 속 미국·영국·프랑스·독일인은 바에서 위스키나 칵테일 한 잔을 들고 서서 이야기만 나눈다. 테이블 가득 안주를 깔아 놓는 우리 술자리와는 사뭇 다르다.

items.title: 셰익스피어 통찰도, 플레밍의 발견도 ‘여기’서 시작됐다
items.snippet: 그 유명한 심리학자 프로이트는 ‘햄릿’을 ‘오이디푸스 콤플렉스’의 전형으로 해석했다. 이 의미심장한 분석 이래 셰익스피어의 작품들은 수많은 심리학자가 지대한 관심을 가지고 연구한 가장 대표적인 대상이다. 수많은 사례가 있지만 몇 가지만 더 예를 들어 보자. 카를 구스타프 융과 후대에 그를 따르는 분석가들은 셰익스피어 작품 ‘폭풍우’의 프로스페로와 주변 인물들을 한 개인의 내면 속 원형(archetype)과 개성화 과정(individuation)으로 해석했다. 프랑스의 정신분석학자 자크 라캉은 ‘햄릿’을 심층 분석해 타인의 욕망을 자신의 욕망으로 착각하는 ‘타자의 욕망을 욕망하는 자아’의 개념을 확립했다. 심지어 셰익스피어의 작품에는 오늘날 정신질환 진단 기준이 되는 ‘DSM(정신질환의 진단 및 통계 매뉴얼)’에 등장하는 다양한 정신질환들이 놀...

items.title: 나 자신에 대한 오해
items.snippet: 우리나라 성인 비만율이 꾸준히 올라가 지난해에는 3명 중 1명꼴로 비만이었다고 합니다. 질병관리청이 며칠 전 발표한 ‘2025 지역사회건강조사’ 심층 분석 결과에 따르면, 지난해 국내 성인의 35.4%가 비만인 것으로 나타났습니다. 이 비율은 2016년보다 7.5%포인트 상승했습니다. 비만은 몸무게(㎏)를 키(m)의 제곱으로 나눈 체질량지수(BMI)가 25 이상인 경우를 말합니다.

items.title: 자연의 부패를 극복한 최고 발명품, ‘냉장 문명’이 녹아내린다면
items.snippet: 새벽 3시 서울 아파트 현관 앞으로 배송된 마트 보랭(保冷) 상자. 아르헨티나산 오징어, 호주 쇠고기, 노르웨이 고등어, 태국 계란, 페루 아보카도, 이탈리아 치즈, 중국 백합, 뉴질랜드 키위와 플로리다 오렌지가 은빛 보랭 포장재에 드라이아이스·얼음팩과 함께 꽁꽁 싸여 있다.

items.title: 버스보다 32년 먼저 등장한 지하철
items.snippet: ‘시민의 발’인 버스와 지하철. 어떤 게 먼저 등장했을까? 버스라고 생각하기 쉽지만, 전 세계에서 지하철은 1863년 처음 운행을 시작했는데 버스는 1895년에야 등장했다.

items.title: 콘서트·영화관·카페가 붐비는 이유? 수면族 때문!
items.snippet: 지난 10일 낮 12시 20분쯤 찾은 서울 강남구 ‘애니파크’. 만화책이나 보드게임 등을 즐기는 멀티카페지만, 이용객 20여 명이 점심시간을 이용해 각자 2평 안팎 방에서 낮잠을 자고 있었다. 카페 입구에는 담요와 쿠션 수십 개가 비치돼 있었다. 직장인 박모(43)씨는 “점심시간에 눈을 붙이고, 간단히 끼니도 해결할 수 있어서 1주일에 2~3번은 온다”고 했다. 카페 관계자는 “낮잠 수요가 많아 올해 초에는 1시간 이용권에 음식과 음료가 포함된 ‘직장인 세트’ 메뉴도 출시했다”고 말했다.

items.title: ‘내향인의 여행’부터 노벨상까지… 스톡홀름을 스쳐만 가선 안 된다
items.snippet: “패키지로 북유럽 여행을 오는 한국 여행객 대부분은 스웨덴에 하루밖에 시간을 내주지 않는다”고 스톡홀름 현지 가이드가 말했다. 실제 핀란드·스웨덴·노르웨이 3국을 방문한다는 북유럽 패키지도 일정을 뜯어보면 스웨덴에는 길어야 1박, 짧으면 반나절 잠시 머무르고 갈 뿐이다.

items.title: 성수동 다음은 서촌·북촌?
items.snippet: 이탈리아 명품 브랜드 보테가 베네타가 팬진(fanzine·브랜드가 직접 발행하는 소규모 잡지) 공개 행사를 서울 서촌 ‘카멜커피’에서 지난 1일까지 보름가량 열었다. 유명 사진작가 유르겐 텔러가 보테가 베네타의 겨울 컬렉션 창작 과정을 포착·기록한 이미지로 꾸민 카페에는 행사 기간 내내 인파가 몰렸다. 매일 선착순 100명에게 나눠준 에코백을 받으려고 이른 새벽부터 길게 줄이 늘어서는 ‘오픈런’이 벌어지기도 했다. 성수동이나 청담동, 대형 백화점에서 주로 열리던 글로벌 명품 브랜드 이벤트가 경복궁을 마주한 로컬 카페에서 열린 것이다. 서촌과 북촌이 서울을 대표하는 새로운 트렌드 중심지로 자리매김하고 있음을 보여주는 상징적인 장면으로 받아들여지고 있다.

items.title: 빨간 양념 위로 번지는 담백함
items.snippet: 시험을 마치면 친구들과 부산대로 향하는 버스를 탔다. 밥을 먹고 노래방에서 놀아볼 심산이었다. 지금은 사라진, 부산대 정문 사거리 지하에 있던 ‘덮밥일번지’가 첫 번째 목적지였다. 계단을 두세 칸씩 건너뛰며 내려갔다. 우리는 식욕만 남은 짐승이었다. 김치, 오징어, 소고기 등을 볶아 올린 덮밥은 그 당시 기준으로도 유난히 싸고 양이 많았다. 따로 나온 멸치 육수를 마시며 숨도 쉬지 않고 숟가락질 하면 종업원 이모들이 멀찍이 지켜보다 ‘참 잘 먹네’ 같은 말을 했다. 그러면 더 의기양양해서 뱃속에 밥을 밀어 넣었다.

items.title: 분노 사회
items.snippet: 얼마 전 층간 소음으로 인한 다툼으로 이웃을 살해한 사건이 발생했습니다. 순간의 분노를 조절하지 못하고 행한 이와 유사한 사건이 빈번하게 발생하고 있습니다. 이로 인해 행위자가 받게 될 중한 처벌과 상대방이 입은 끔찍한 피해, 그리고 양쪽 가족들이 겪을 고통을 생각하면 참으로 안타깝습니다. 최근에는 분노한 나머지 복수할 목적으로 제3자에게 테러를 의뢰하고, 제3자는 돈을 받고 테러를 대행해주는 기상천외의 범죄까지 등장했습니다. 또한, 마치 사설 구난차가 사고 현장에 빠르게 도착해서 이득을 얻는 것처럼 사회적 분노를 일으킬 만한 타인의 행적을 찾아내어 인터넷에 영상의 형태로 공론화해서 이득(조회 수, 광고 수익 등)을 챙기는, 이른바 사이버 렉카도 늘어나고 있습니다. 이처럼 분노가 적절히 조절되지 못해 불행한 사태가 생기고, 타인의 분노를 이용...

items.title: “켄차나~” “알았어데스!”를 대하는 우리의 자세
items.snippet: 외래어와 외국어의 홍수는 해가 바뀌고 계절이 바뀌어도 멈출 줄 모르는데 ‘외거어(外去語)’와 ‘한본어(韓本語)’ 소식이 가물에 콩 나는 것 이상으로 들려온다. 외거어는 우리말이 다른 언어에 들어가 쓰이는 말이고, 한본어는 우리말이 일본에 들어가 일본어와 섞여 쓰이고 있는 말이다. ‘오빠(oppa)’와 ‘언니(unni)’들이 해외에서 ‘대박(daebak)’을 낸 덕에 들려오는 소식이 고마우면서도 다른 한편으로는 말에 대한 이중적인 태도를 다시금 돌아보게 된다.

items.title: 우리가 아는 다빈치의 얼굴, 누가 그렸을까
items.snippet: “그는 제게 훌륭한 아버지 같은 분이셨습니다. 제가 느끼는 슬픔은 이루 말할 수 없습니다. 살아 있는 한 저는 오래도록 이 슬픔을 안고 살아갈 것입니다.” 1519년 6월 1일, 프란체스코 멜치(Melzi)가 레오나르도 다빈치(da Vinci)의 형제들에게 보낸 편지의 한 대목이다. 스승을 잃은 제자는 비통한 상실감을 편지에 담았다. 한 달 전, 다빈치는 프랑스 앙부아즈의 클로 뤼세 저택에서 예순일곱 살로 생을 마감했다. 그는 죽음을 앞두고 공증인 앞에서 유언을 남겼다. 평생의 관찰과 연구가 담긴 노트와 드로잉, 회화 도구를 멜치에게 물려준다는 내용이었다. 당대 최고의 거장은 왜 혈육을 배제하고 젊은 제자에게 소중한 기록들을 맡겼을까. 멜치는 어떤 사람이었기에 다빈치의 절대적인 신뢰를 얻었을까.

items.title: 억울한 사람 구하라고 만든 법, 입 막는 데 쓰여서야
items.snippet: 2018년 3월 새벽, 뮤지컬 배우 강은일은 서울의 한 순댓국집에서 지인과 지인의 고교동창 A씨 등 다수와 술자리를 갖는다. 하지만 그 자리는 강씨에게 몇 년에 걸친 엄청난 비극의 서막이 되고 만다. A의 성범죄 무고로 피해를 본 것이다. A의 주장에 따르면 그날 강씨는 화장실에 들어간 A의 허리를 한 손으로 감싼 뒤 다른 한 손으로 가슴을 만지며 강제로 입맞춤했단다. 이 음식점 화장실은 출입문을 열고 들어가면 왼쪽은 여자, 오른쪽은 남자 칸으로 나뉘어 있고 가운데 세면대가 있는 구조였다. 강씨는 자신이 용변을 보고 세면대에서 손을 씻는데 A가 다짜고짜 스킨십을 했다고 반박한다. A를 바로 밀쳐냈지만, 그녀는 강씨에게 “가족관계는 어떻게 되냐” “집에 돈 많냐” 등 이상한 질문을 했다는 것이다. 일행이 화장실에 와서 두 사람을 떼어냈고 사건이...

items.title: 손흥민·96라인 손잡았지만... 사우디에 21년 만의 충격패
items.snippet: 한국 축구 대표팀을 이끄는 로베르트 모레노 임시 감독의 첫 원정길이 패배로 끝났다. 그것도 21년 만의 기록적인 패배다.

items.title: Microsoft’s global outage may be worse than Amazon's or CrowdStrike's, expert says
items.snippet: Governments, hospitals, courts scrambled by global Microsoft outage.

items.title: 하이트진로, 3분기 영업익 577억원…예상치 부합
items.snippet: 하이트진로가 올해 3분기 시장 기대에 부합하는 영업이익을 거뒀다. 주류 시장 위축에도 수익성 중심의 경영 전략을 이어온 결과다.하이트진로[000080]는 13일 분기보고서를 공시하고 3분기 연결 기준 매출액 6천324억 원, 영업이익 577억 원을 거뒀다고 밝혔다.전년 동기 대비 매출액은 5.5% 줄었지만 영업이익은 6.2% 늘었다.3분기 실적은 시장 기대에 부합했다.연합인포맥스가 최근 두 달 내 국내 증권사 3곳이 제출한 실적 전망치를 집계한 결과, 하이트진로는 3분기 연결 기준 매출액 6천440억 원, 영업이익 568억 원을

items.title: Close-up Photographer of the Year 2026 unveils shortlist of extraordinary nature images

items.title: 조현, 중국에 '한반도 문제' 역할 당부…왕이 "정책 변함없어"

items.title: AnalogLayoutWorld: An Open Benchmark for Agentic Analog Layout Design
items.abstract: Coding agents have demonstrated strong capabilities in software development, yet their ability to tackle long-horizon engineering tasks governed by physical constraints remains less understood. We study this question through analog circuit layout, which demands domain knowledge, geometric reasoning, and iterative interaction with design and verification tools. We introduce \textbf{AnalogLayoutWorld}, an open-source agent benchmark with 40 expert-reviewed tasks for end-to-end layout generation from fixed transistor-level netlists. It combines an integrated design environment with independent physical and post-layout electrical verification, as well as objective layout quality metrics co-designed with analog layout experts. items.snippet: 서울북부지방공소청은 12일 청소년 A(15)양을 살해한 혐의로 진모(59)씨에 대해 구속영장을 청구했다. 진씨는 지난 10일 저녁 공유 숙박 앱에서 얻은 성북구 정릉동의 한 주택에서 A양을 흉기로 살해한 혐의를 받는다. 범행 직후 진씨는 내연녀 김모(26)씨에게 전화를 걸어 “내가 사람을 죽였고 나도 죽을 것”이라고 말했다고 한다. 서울 성북경찰서가 11일 새벽 1시 25분 김씨 신고를 받고 출동해보니 진씨는 술에 취해 있었고 A양은 피를 흘린 채 숨진 상태였다. 현장에서는 빈 소주병 3개와 불을 붙이지 않은 번개탄, 진씨가 작성한 유서도 발견됐다.

items.title: Interfacial Effects of Thermal Reorganization on Charge and Spin Transport in Organic Spin Valves
items.abstract: Organic semiconductors are attractive for spintronic applications owing to their weak spin-orbit coupling, small hyperfine interactions, mechanical flexibility, and tunable electronic properties. Organic spin valves (OSVs) provide a representative platform for investigating spin-dependent transport. However, the magnetoresistance (MR) response is highly sensitive to the ferromagnetic electrode/organic semiconductor interface (spinterface). Variations in interfacial morphology, chemical interaction, energy-level alignment, and spin polarization can strongly affect spin injection, transport, and detection, making reproducible OSV performance difficult to achieve. Here, we investigate how in situ thermal annealing affects the electrical and magnetotransport properties of complete NDI-based OSVs. items.title: Gatemon qubits based on in-situ ternary InAsSb/Al nanowire Josephson junctions
items.abstract: Ternary InAsSb/Al nanowires combine compositionally engineerable semiconductor properties with epitaxial proximity superconductivity, making them attractive for hybrid quantum circuits and mesoscopic superconductivity. Here, we realize gatemon qubits based on shadow-defined in-situ InAsSb/Al Josephson junctions in a single growth process. Gate-dependent microwave spectroscopy demonstrates electrostatic tuning of the qubit transition over several gigahertz. Rabi oscillations and Ramsey interference show coherent qubit control, with representative values T1 = 0.79 us and T2* = 0.91 us. Across five gatemons distributed over three chips, the measured relaxation times range from approximately 0.2 us to 1 us and decrease with increasing qubit frequency. Their magnitude is comparable to a circuit estimate of spontaneous emission into the electromagnetic environment. These results establish in-s...

items.title: Progress on the MALTA CMOS Sensor: Edge-TCT Measurements for Parametric Pixel Simulation
items.abstract: MALTA2 is a monolithic active pixel sensor, developed in the 180 nm CMOS imaging technology for radiation-hard applications in high-rate environments. This contribution summarizes recent developments in the characterization and simulation of MALTA2. The charge collection of a sensor on epitaxial silicon is studied with the Edge Transient Current Technique (Edge-TCT), using a digital readout, where the charge is reconstructed solely from binary hit data. In previous works, only specially designed analog output pixels at the matrix periphery were investigated. In contrast, the digital readout gives access to the full edge of the pixel matrix. Laser scans across neighboring pixels enable a two-dimensional parameterization of the charge collection. items.title: Bright and Uniform Silicon Carbide Nanophotonic Arrays for Scalable Nanoscale Quantum Sensing
items.abstract: Silicon carbide (SiC) spin defects are emerging as powerful platforms for nanoscale quantum sensing due to their near-surface stability, near-infrared emission, and CMOS compatibility. However, poor photon collection efficiency and the reliance on randomly distributed defects hinder the realization of practical, large-scale devices. Here, we demonstrate scalable, ultra-bright, and highly uniform SiC quantum nanophotonic arrays. By combining a self-aligned fabrication process with localized oxygen ion implantation, we deterministically position PL5 and PL6 centers at the exact center of 4H-SiC nanopillars. This architecture yields record-high photon count rates of $\sim$1 Mcps (PL5) and $\sim$2 Mcps (PL6), establishing a new benchmark for SiC color centers while maintaining near-identical brightness across the array. items.title: High-Quality InSb Nanowires Grown by Molecular-Beam Epitaxy via Precise Catalyst Modulation
items.abstract: Semiconductor InSb nanowires are a major material candidate for topological quantum computation. The nanowires in current devices were mostly grown using metal organic chemical vapor deposition, incompatible with in situ growth of superconductor, a crucial requirement for low-disorder devices. Growth of InSb nanowires using molecular-beam epitaxy (MBE) can address this issue. So far, studies on MBE-grown InSb remain limited due to an extremely narrow parameter window for the growth and reproducibility. Moreover, the use of foreign catalysts can introduce deep-level impurities. Here, we report a self-catalyzed MBE growth of InSb nanowires without those foreign catalysts. We first grow GaAs nanowire stems, and then convert Ga catalyst droplets into In droplets in situ. Axial heteroepitaxial growth of InSb can be realized through the In droplets on top of GaAs stems. items.title: Self-Supervised Attention-Based Virtual Metrology for CMP MRR Prediction
items.abstract: Chemical mechanical planarization (CMP) is a critical semiconductor manufacturing process where material removal rate (MRR) is a key metric for process monitoring and advanced process control (APC). Virtual metrology enables MRR estimation from process time series signals, supporting run-to-run(R2R) control and process optimization while reducing reliance on physical metrology. Existing approaches typically rely on simplified linear assumptions or require handcrafted feature engineering. In this paper, we propose Global Regression Pretraining(GREP), a self-supervised, attention-based framework for CMP MRR prediction. GREP learns temporal representations from unlabeled sensor signals through global proxy-target regression, followed by supervised fine-tuning for MRR estimation. items.title: Integrated optical isolators enabled by 2D semiconductors via spin-momentum locking
items.abstract: Integrated optical isolators based on spin-momentum locking hold great potential for protecting photonic integrated circuits from unwanted reflections. Currently, the most common implementations are magneto-optical isolators that require an externally applied magnetic field. Nevertheless, a wide range of nonreciprocal effects remains to be exploited in alternative material platforms. Although the majority of these effects induce changes to the propagation of light as a function of its polarization, they can be directly connected to the propagation direction through spin-momentum locking. We employ a computational approach to investigate various designs of integrated isolators based on nonreciprocal 2D semiconductors, studying the influence of their geometry and optical properties on the device performance. items.title: Quantum geometric bounds and uncertainty relations for velocity variance and spread of Wannier function
items.abstract: By utilizing the derivation of quantum Cramér-Rao bound and an argument put forward by Efimov and Dodonov, we derive several uncertainty relations for mixed states that constrain the diagonal product, trace, and each diagonal element of the covariance matrix of multiple observables. By choosing the observables to be the symmetric logarithmic derivative, the uncertainty relations imply various geometric bounds on quantum Fisher information matrix caused by mean Uhlmann curvature, which in pure states become geometric bounds on quantum metric caused by Berry curvature. Our formalism reveals optical sum rules for velocity variance and spread of valence band Wannier functions, and how they are bounded by the Berry curvature and commutator of velocity operators. items.title: Development and characterization of monolithic sensors with internal gain in a 110 nm CMOS process
items.abstract: This paper presents the optimization and characterization of a Monolithic Active Pixel Sensor with internal gain implemented in the 110 nm CMOS process from LFoundry. This work, carried out within the framework of the latest ARCADIA production run, reports on the characterization of sensors with an optimized gain layer. Improvements over earlier prototypes, including substrate current reduction via guard-ring connection, are briefly discussed. Both laboratory and in-beam measurements are presented. Using soft X-rays from a 55Fe source, both the pixel response and the noise performance are analyzed. In addition, laser measurements demonstrate an electronic jitter ranging from 20 to 40 ps for a signal amplitude corresponding to one minimum ionizing particle (MIP). items.title: Large-scale characterisation of silicon T centres with tuning-free broadband cavities
items.abstract: T centres in silicon combine an optical transition in the telecom O-band with a long-lived electron and nuclear spin in a photonics- and CMOS-compatible host. However, weak emission of photons in the zero-phonon line (ZPL) makes measurements slow. Cavities can increase the ZPL photon emission, but high-Q cavities require individual tuning to the T centre wavelength, hindering statistical understanding of T centre properties. Here, we overcome this limitation by developing low-Q confocally-addressable cavities. We create an array of 400 cavities, detuned $0.0\pm 1.1$ nm from the T centre, with an average quality factor of $298\pm 78$. The combination of high accuracy and moderate quality factors removes the need for individual tuning. items.title: Nitride crystalline barrier epitaxial SIS Josephson junctions by MBE
items.abstract: Superconductor-insulator-superconductor Josephson junctions with crystalline tunnel barriers have remained elusive by epitaxial techniques such as MOCVD or MBE that produce the junction materials and devices powering today's electronic and photonic systems like transistors and lasers. Here, we overcome the key materials hurdle to realize the first functional nitride crystalline barrier Josephson junctions by MBE. Despite an AlN barrier thickness of approximately 4.5 nm, the NbN/AlN/NbN trilayers exhibit coherent Josephson tunneling with critical current densities of approximately 17 A/cm2, an IcRn product of approximately 2.5 mV, and a superconducting gap voltage of approximately 3.7 mV with a BCS-like gap evolution with temperature. items.title: Distilling an atomistic foundation model is all you need for large-scale molecular dynamics of semiconductor interfaces
items.abstract: State-of-the-art atomistic foundation models provide broadly transferable energy and force predictions, but their direct deployment in large-scale molecular dynamics remains computationally costly. Here we examine whether their knowledge can be distilled into compact potentials while retaining the physical responses of heterogeneous semiconductor interfaces. From 128 pretrained models spanning 22 model families, we select a fixed EquiformerV3 teacher and train atomic cluster expansion (ACE) and neuroevolution potential (NEP) students without target-specific teacher fine-tuning, with both simulation speed and accessible system size improved by several orders of magnitude relative to the teacher model. items.title: Correlation-Consistent Gaussian Basis Sets for Periodic Solids. I. Hydrogen and p-block Elements from Boron to Chlorine
items.abstract: We present the cc-pVXZ-s series (X = D, T, and Q) of correlation-consistent Gaussian basis sets for solids, covering hydrogen and the p-block elements from boron to chlorine. The series includes basis sets of consistent quality for the all-electron potential and for various pseudopotentials and effective core potentials commonly used in periodic calculations. Our design combines Dunning's construction of the molecular cc-pVXZ series with a revised material-constrained atomic optimization (MCAO) algorithm for improved numerical performance. MCAO regularizes standard atomic optimization to suppress overly diffuse basis functions and ensure numerical stability in a set of reference solids. items.title: Squeezed Light Generation by Cooper Pair Recombination in a Superconductor-Semiconductor Structure
items.abstract: We theoretically demonstrate squeezed light generation in a compact, electrically driven device utilizing the nonlinear light-matter interaction of Cooper-pair recombination in a hybrid superconductorsemiconductor structure. On the basis of second-order perturbation theory, we developed an effective Hamiltonian which incorporates the electronic component of the interaction as a photon coupling strength coefficient, enabling a model to describe the quadrature squeezing effect of Cooper-pair recombination on the photonic state. We find the squeezing strength to be proportional to the superconducting energy gap squared and device length, as well as increasing with applied voltage. For practical device length, materials and voltage bias, we calculated squeezing values comparable to those of existing squeezed light generation methods when operating below the critical temperature. items.title: Quantum Thermal Transistor via Nonlinear Environmental Coupling
items.abstract: Thermal amplification enables sensitive control of heat currents, providing a basis for heat management and thermal signal processing in quantum devices. For a harmonic oscillator coupled to emitter, collector, and base thermal reservoirs, we recover the absence of thermal amplification when system-reservoir interactions permit only single-quantum exchange. A controlled weak-nonlinearity expansion, supported by numerical stationary solutions, shows that two-quantum exchange at the emitter enables amplification and predicts its onset. When two-quantum exchange dominates at the emitter and collector, varying the base temperature redistributes populations between even and odd oscillator sectors. This changes the emitter and collector heat currents far more than the base current, enabling large thermal amplification. items.title: Analysis and Demonstration of a Current-Stiff, Isolated Capacitive Bridge Transformer
items.abstract: The traditional Voltage Source Inverter (VSI) based Dual Active Bridge (DAB) utilizes a transformer at its center to provide galvanic isolation and a turns ratio for step up/down functionality. However, the transformer is often the limiting factor of the DAB, especially as semiconductor switching speeds improve, given steel core losses, winding losses, etc. This paper presents a new DAB architecture based on Current Source Inverters (CSIs) coupled through, and isolated by, an AC capacitive bridge, yielding a system called a Capacitive Bridge Transformer (CBT). The CBT architecture eliminates all magnetic components in the AC portion of the isolated DAB circuit, reducing frequency scaling barriers normally present in DABs. items.abstract: Semiconductor nanostructures are key light-management elements because their geometry can strengthen light-matter interaction, suppress reflection, and enhance optical coupling. items.title: SLIC: Reinforcement Fine-Tuning Small LMs for Multi-Turn Analog Circuit Optimization
items.abstract: Analog integrated circuit (IC) design is a multi-turn, simulator-grounded engineering task that demands iterative reasoning over coupled performance tradeoffs, yet proprietary process design kits (PDKs) make hosted large language model workflows difficult to deploy in practical design settings. We present SLIC (Small LM Iterating on Circuits), a reinforcement fine-tuning framework that trains a 4B-scale, locally deployable language model for closed-loop analog circuit optimization. SLIC pairs structured circuit representations with discretized relative-update actions, domain- and success-gated multiobjective rewards, and Reward-Guided Rollout Steering (RGRS), which turns per-step simulator feedback into signals for both policy learning and online rollout construction in this sparse, highly constrained domain. items.title: 5G CATS: 5G-Based Cryptographic Authorization Against Trafficking of Semiconductor Devices
items.abstract: Enforcing export controls on AI accelerators requires verifying where a chip operates after deployment. Round-trip time measurements can bound a chip's distance from a trusted landmark, but any jitter in honest replies forces the verifier to loosen its timeout, giving an attacker slack to relay traffic over fiber from a restricted region. Prior approaches either cross the untrusted host stack or rely on noisy power-line channels that inflate this slack. We present 5G CATS, a location certification system that pairs a co-packaged 5G radio, cryptographic engine, and hardware interlock on the GPU package with 5G Ultra-Reliable Low-Latency Communication (URLLC) base stations. Terminating the radio link inside the package removes the host software, PCIe fabric, and baseboard management controller from the verification path. items.title: Ultrafast Hole Transport and Electron Localization in Superatomic Re$_{6}$Se$_{8}$Cl$_{2}$
items.abstract: Van der Waals superatomic crystals represent an intriguing class of materials, exhibiting unique ultrafast electronic and structural responses arising from their hierarchical crystal structure. These materials bridge the properties of semiconductors, molecular solids, and nanocrystal arrays, hosting a range of many-body interactions that can be controlled with atomically precise structures. To establish the structure-function correlation, it is necessary to understand element-specific electronic states arising from complex superatomic unit cells. Here, we use transient XUV spectroscopy to individually probe the dynamics of photoexcited electrons and holes in Re$_{6}$Se$_{8}$Cl$_{2}$ superatomic crystals. items.title: The Weight Is in the Reading: Hidden States in Memristors, Memlumors, and Electrochemical Transistors
items.abstract: Physical synapses are routinely described by a single number, the weight, that is identified with a conductance, a current, or a luminescence yield. This identification conflates two different objects: the internal state that the device stores, and the signal obtained when that state is read. Building on Chua's formulation of memristive systems, we separate the state variable, which evolves with the excitation history, from the observation map that converts it into a measured signal, and we define the weight as the outcome of a specified read protocol. Three platforms show the consequences: a memristor, in which the same voltage writes and reads; a memlumor, in which light both modifies the state and produces the photoluminescence that reports it; and an organic electrochemical transistor (OECT), in which the gate writes and the channel reads. items.title: Ground-state phase diagram of the spin-1/2 Heisenberg zigzag ladder with anisotropic $Γ$ term revisited
items.abstract: We study the spin-1/2 Heisenberg antiferromagnet with an anisotropic $Γ$ term on a zigzag ladder, which can be exactly mapped to the spin-1/2 XYZ zigzag ladder by a spin rotation. This model has recently attracted considerable interest as an effective model for the quasi-one-dimensional magnetic semiconductor YbCuS$_2$. For the model, the ground-state phase diagram was previously proposed by Saito and Hotta [Phys. Rev. Lett. 132, 166701 (2024); Phys. Rev. B 110, 024409 (2024)]. We systematically reexamine the phase diagram through complementary numerical and analytical approaches, including exact diagonalization, the density-matrix renormalization group method, and low-energy effective theories. items.title: Neutronic Field-Effect Transistor
items.abstract: Field-effect electronic devices are in widespread use in communication, computing, data storage, and sensing applications. We demonstrate a neutronic field-effect transistor (NFET) that is analogous to the Datta-Das electron spin transistor and atomtronic devices. The NFET is based on a perfect-crystal Mach-Zehnder neutron interferometer with phase shifts applied to the spin and path degrees of freedom.

items.title: Spin-valve effect through electrostatic coupling
items.abstract: We propose a spin-valve effect in which an insulating magnetic van der Waals multilayer controls the conductance of an adjacent non-magnetic conductor by electrostatic coupling, without transport-electrons entering the magnetic layers. The coupling is induced by the variations of the electronic structure when the relative orientation of the magnetization of adjacent monolayers changes from parallel to antiparallel, modifying both the dielectric constant and band alignment. We consider two types of coupling and device concepts: charge transfer to a graphene monolayer and capacitive coupling in a single-electron transistor. We use density functional calculations to assess the magnitude of the effect in various materials, including CrI$_3$, CrBr$_3$, CrCl$_3$ and NiBr$_2$. items.title: Gate-tunable supercurrent switching in a three-terminal quantum dot transistor
items.abstract: We propose and analyze a three-terminal superconducting transistor switch in which a gate-defined quantum dot region interrupts a flux-controlled loop. The output supercurrent is switched off completely when the two loop arms couple to the dot with equal tunneling strengths and half a flux quantum threads the loop. The device then operates as a symmetric SQUID at half flux. The condition follows from a single geometric factor $χ$, which reduces the three-terminal problem to an equivalent two-terminal Anderson impurity model and makes the switching mechanism independent of the Coulomb interaction, the dot level position, the total hybridization and temperature. These enter only through a prefactor and thus decide how tolerant the device is to imperfect barrier tuning. items.title: Impact of multi-dot configurations on electron temperature and double quantum dot latching in gate-controlled qubit devices
items.abstract: Many currently envisaged scalable architectures for Si/SiGe spin qubit devices utilize gate-controlled multi-dot configurations characterized by their peculiar Coulomb blockade physics. One example is the concurrent use of a single electron transistor (SET) as a charge sensor and as a reservoir for adjacent qubit quantum dots (QD). We find that the SET energy spectrum impacts pulsed gate spectroscopy of the QD when the SET simultaneously acts as the reservoir and the sensor. Then, using the qubit QD as a probe, we quantify how strongly the electron temperature of the SET depends on the applied bias. It surpasses a reference experiment by 100 $mK$ even at 50 $μV$ bias. Our results provide a strong incentive for choosing spin qubit initialization schemes which do not rely on coupling to the reservoir in such devices. items.title: Environmental Assessment of GaN Current-Source and Voltage-Source AC-AC Variable Speed Drives
items.abstract: Three-phase ac-ac converters for variable-speed drives can be realized conventionally as voltage-source converters (VSCs) or, leveraging emerging monolithic bidirectional GaN power transistors (M-BDSs), as current-source converters (CSCs). This paper presents a comparative life-cycle assessment of a realized VSC and a CSC demonstrators including grid-side and motor-side EMI filters, and with identical specifications (1.4 kW rated power, 200 V line-to-line rms grid and motor voltage). The embodied carbon footprints are similar (44.8 kgCO2eq for the VSC and 47.4 kgCO2eq for the CSC) and dominated by auxiliary and control electronics, and the printed circuit boards. items.title: Rapid Heat Removal from Chip Cores: Near-Junction Active Cooling of Power Transistors via Electron Entropy Transport and Spatial Decoupling
items.abstract: Chip performance is limited by a shared bottleneck: the core produces heat faster than it can be moved out. We study the hardest case, RF power GaN HEMTs, whose hotspots exceed 5 kW/cm^2, and propose a horizontal near-junction active cooling topology built on electron entropy transport. Classical on-chip thermoelectric cooling faces a contest: Peltier absorption grows linearly with current, Joule heating with its square. In a vertical pillar, its own conduction resistance locks about half the Joule heat back toward the cold end, capping net cooling. From the Onsager framework we show the origin of this asymmetry: Peltier absorption localizes at the interface where the Seebeck coefficient jumps, whereas Joule heating fills the volume. items.title: Orbital texture of valence band and interband transitions of the type-II multiferroic van der Waals NiI$_2$
items.abstract: NiI$_2$ is a van der Waals semiconductor characterized by complex electronic and magnetic phases, holding promise towards functional applications. For this purpose, a detailed understanding of its band structure and its excitations is essential to elucidate the electronic and transport properties. We present a comprehensive description of the band structure and of the lowest valence-to-conduction band transition in bulk NiI$_2$, by means of time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy supported by first-principles calculations. We describe the orbital character of Ni and I manifolds, and identify the main momentum-resolved features of the valence band and the shallow minima of the conduction band. With this study, we provide a foundational understanding of the electronic structure of NiI$_2$ and its single-particle interband electronic excitation, a benchmark for theoretical model...

items.title: A Per-Step Load-Balancing Engine for Expert-Parallel MoE Serving
items.abstract: In expert-parallel Mixture-of-Experts serving, a layer finishes only when the most loaded GPU of its group does. Token routing shifts at every decode step and concentrates on a few experts, so most of the group's reserved GPU time waits on stragglers. Recovering that time means re-deciding, at every layer of every decode step, how each replicated expert's tokens divide between its copies. The exact linear-program solvers that make this decision optimally take longer than many of the layers they serve, and their working set outgrows GPU shared memory at deployment scale. We introduce Relief, a bidirectional pairwise relaxation that makes the linear program unnecessary, coming within a fraction of a point of the per-step optimum in a few passes of integer halving over the token counts. ICLayout-Bench is a benchmark in which agents use electronic design automation (EDA) tools to construct and optimize GDSII layouts from transistor-level circuit netlists. These layouts are evaluated using physical verification, parasitic extraction, and post-layout simulation. The benchmark includes 165 tasks across 13 process design kits (PDKs), covering technology nodes from 3 nm to 180 nm. items.title: $>3\text{ W/mm}$ Output Power $\mathrm{Al}_{0.61}\mathrm{Ga}_{0.39}\mathrm{N}$ Channel HEMT with $24.4\%$ Associated PAE at $10\text{ GHz}$
items.abstract: In this work, an ultra-wide bandgap (UWBG) high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT) was fabricated using an $\mathrm{Al}_{0.76}\mathrm{Ga}_{0.24}\mathrm{N}$ barrier and an $\mathrm{Al}_{0.61}\mathrm{Ga}_{0.39}\mathrm{N}$ channel with thick $\mathrm{SiO}_2$ passivation. The device demonstrated low current collapse at $40\text{ V}$ drain bias. At $10\text{ GHz}$, the device exhibited an output power of $3.07\text{ W/mm}$ with an associated power-added efficiency (PAE) of $24.4\%$. A peak PAE of $33.9\%$ was achieved at an associated output power of $2.14\text{ W/mm}$. This excellent large-signal performance highlights the strong potential of UWBG $\mathrm{AlGaN}$ channel devices for X-band applications.

The devices featured a recessed T-gate structure and $\mathrm{SiO_2}$ passivation. items.title: Deterministically fabricated C-band single-photon sources based on quantum dot circular Bragg grating cavities
items.abstract: Telecom-wavelength quantum light sources are essential components for scalable fiber-based quantum networks, where on-demand emission of single photons is required for high secret key rates. Here, we demonstrate the deterministic integration of metal-organic vapor-phase epitaxy (MOVPE)-grown C-band InAs/InP quantum dots into circular Bragg grating resonators. The integrated emitters exhibit a radiative lifetime of $T_1 = (1400 \pm 50)~\mathrm{ps}$ and a spectral linewidth of $ΔE_{\mathrm{FWHM}} = (41.0 \pm 4.0)~μ\mathrm{eV}$. Under non-resonant excitation, we measure a post-selected single-photon purity of $(0.95 \pm 0.02)$ and a raw two-photon interference visibility of $V_{12\mathrm{ns}} = (35 \pm 2)\%$, which increases to $(70 \pm 18)\%$ under temporal post-selection. items.title: Wafer-scale MoS2 and HZO-based Ferroelectric Field Effect Transistors with 4.4 V Memory Window for Back-End Compatible Multibit Memory

Polycrystalline In2O3-based TFTs are promising candidates; however, conventional flexible substrates such as plastics are not suitable because their fabrication typically requires relatively high temperatures (~350 deg.C). In this study, we used mica as a flexible substrate to fabricate polycrystalline In2O3-based TFTs, motivated by previous demonstrations of crystalline oxide growth on mica. The resulting TFTs exhibited a uFE of approximately 75 cm^2/Vs. The devices maintained gate-modulated operation after 10^3 flex-out bending cycles at a 5 mm radius, whereas flex-in cycling caused early electrical failure, likely due to In2O3 film degradation. items.title: How light interacts with matter, revisited
items.abstract: In 1968 Victor Weisskopf explained in Scientific American how light interacts with matter, with a few formulas and many words. We tell the same story again with the tools that have since become available: the fields are computed and drawn, and their evolution in time is shown in animations. Light is described as a classical electromagnetic field and matter as a collection of charged oscillators; every phenomenon follows from adding up the retarded waves radiated by the oscillators, each with its proper delay and phase. From this single picture we obtain the blue of the sky and the white of the clouds, transparency and the refractive index, the Ewald-Oseen extinction theorem, reflection and the colours of thin films, why metals reflect and what gives metals and semiconductors their colours, polarizers, Brewster's angle and birefringence, the working of mirrors, lenses, microscopes and the...

items.abstract: Logical qubits encoded in collective states of multiple spins are promising building blocks for large-scale semiconductor quantum processors. As novel fault-tolerant architectures increasingly rely on qubit shuttling, understanding decoherence of the shuttled multi-spin qubits becomes crucial. We analyze fidelity and leakage of the logical qubits dephased by the spatio-temporally correlated $1/f$ noise, considering two-, three-, and four-spin encodings. We study different shuttling protocols and establish that for all encodings generally, parallel shuttling provides the best protection against decoherence at short distances, whereas sequential shuttling outperforms others for long-range transport (although the exact boundaries depend on the specific device parameters). We explain this common behavior in terms of the dephasing factors of pairs of the shuttled spins; we provide explicit ex...

items.title: Discrete time crystals and heteroclinic switching in actively mode-locked semiconductor lasers
items.abstract: We investigate the mechanisms underlying the emergence of discrete time crystals in actively mode-locked semiconductor lasers. Our analysis is based on a Haus master equation generalized to retain carrier memory between round-trips. We perform a detailed bifurcation analysis that reveals a well-defined hierarchy of subharmonic states, illustrating how pulses may suppress their neighbors when the modulation runs faster than the pulse round-trip frequency. To identify the underlying mechanism, we derive effective equations of motion that couple the pulse energies, their positions relative to the modulation transmission maxima, and the local time-dependent gain. These reveal that transitions between time-crystalline states occur via transcritical global bifurcations, opening a regime of heteroclinic winnerless competition between symmetry-degenerate configurations.

items.abstract: Polarons are composite quasiparticles formed when charge carriers strongly couple to lattice vibrations, manifesting as carriers dressed by a surrounding cloud of phonons. Although this dressing fundamentally renormalizes the effective mass and mobility of carriers, its impact on electrically neutral exciton polarons in 2D semiconductors has received limited attention. In particular, despite the growing interest in polaronic effects in atomically thin semiconductors, only a few theoretical studies have addressed spectral signatures and renormalized properties of exciton polarons in these materials. Here, we develop a microscopic model to describe exciton polarons in transition metal dichalcogenides. Applying this model to $1s$ acoustic polarons in an MoSe$_2$ monolayer, we reveal a distinct kink in the polaron dispersion, accompanied by a pronounced broadening of its spectral function. T...

items.abstract: Excitons carry energy and information through a semiconductor without carrying charge. This makes them attractive for optoelectronics, but also hard to guide. Magnetic skyrmions, on the other hand, are moved by small electrical currents. Here we develop a theory of excitons interacting with a skyrmion in which the electron and the hole are treated as distinct constituents, each with its own spin--orbit coupling. We find that the topology of the skyrmion is transferred to the exciton only when the exchange coupling exceeds the relevant spin--orbit splitting. The exciton then experiences a full flux quantum, with opposite signs in the two valleys. The quantum metric of the spin texture creates a ring-shaped barrier that traps excitons, whereas the topological charge fixes the angular momentum of the trapped states and hence their optical selection rules. This paper reviews recent progress in characterizing large format detector at the micropixel scale level, calibrating optical distortion using reference stars, and refining differential astrometry methods to detect the faint astrometric signatures of Earth-mass exoplanets. We highlight the latest developments in the RETINA project, which aims to advance the TRL of GIGAPYX 220 MP CMOS detectors from Pyxalis which are critical components for future space missions such as ESA's Theia and NASA's Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO). items.title: On the collective flow puzzle in ultra-central heavy-ion collisions
items.abstract: Using UCC-DiffHIC, an AI-accelerated event-by-event hydrodynamic model validated against hybrid simula- tions, we study flow in ultracentral Pb-Pb collisions. For suitable initial conditions, the calculated v2{2}/v3{2} approaches unity in the most central collisions, consistent with experiment. An exact response decomposition shows that residual fluctuations suppress the ratio through P3/P2 < 1, where P2 and P3 are Pearson response correlations for elliptic and triangular flow, respectively. This resolves the apparent flow hierarchy without requiring a breakdown of linear response or additional effects such as nuclear deformation.

items.title: A Neural Physics Solver for Richards Equation
items.abstract: A new approach to discretise and solve Richards equation based on the finite element method (FEM) is presented. The Neural Physics method is demonstrated for two different discretisations of Richards equation, including a multigrid method that is realised through a U-Net architecture. items.title: Near-Quantum-Limited Readout for the Princeton Axion Search using a sub-GHz Kinetic Inductance Traveling Wave Parametric Amplifier
items.abstract: Parametric amplifiers are a workhorse for near-quantum-limited measurements above 1 GHz. However, amplifier development has been more limited below 1 GHz. We present a kinetic inductance traveling-wave parametric amplifier (KI-TWPA) operating over 300-700 MHz, with gain exceeding 30 dB and pump powers of a few hundred nanowatts. items.title: Time-resolved infrared spectroscopy with entangled photons and visible-light detection
items.abstract: Time-resolved infrared (TR-IR) spectroscopy reveals molecular structural changes and charge-carrier dynamics on their intrinsic timescales, in photosynthesis, catalysis and optoelectronic materials, but requires complex sources of ultrashort infrared pulses, cryogenically cooled detectors to overcome thermal background, and intense probes that can perturb the sample. Quantum infrared spectroscopy avoids these constraints: harnessing quantum interference between the generation processes of frequency-entangled photon pairs, it reads out the infrared response of a sample by detecting only the visible partner photon, for which efficient detectors exist. To date, it has been limited to steady-state measurements. Here we demonstrate its ultrafast, time-resolved form with a picosecond visible pump pulse and a silicon detector. Each visible pulse generates photon pairs within a picosecond window...

items.title: DefectSkills: Guiding AI agents through first-principles calculations for point defects in semiconductors and insulators
items.abstract: First-principles defect calculations can now be performed autonomously by AI agents, enabled by established computational methods and open-source Python toolkits. items.title: PINND: Physics Informed Neural Networks for Solving the Drift-Diffusion Equations
items.abstract: The drift-diffusion equations are the fundamental building block for the modeling, design, and optimization of modern semiconductor devices. Solutions of the drift-diffusion equations rarely give way to analytical forms, and exhibit strong nonlinearity, with the solutions ranging over several orders of magnitude. These attributes have led to research into numerical solvers, and while many commercial Technology Computer Aided Design (TCAD) packages now exist, they may require long simulation times, exhibit sensitivity to initial guesses, and rely on mesh generation. Further, these solvers are not well suited for inverse problems where the design parameters of a device are retrieved from its desired functional characteristics. To address all these challenges, this work demonstrates the usage of Physics Informed Neural Networks for the Drift-diffusion (PINND) equations with errors comparabl...

items.title: HAWK: Heterogeneity-Aware KV Cache Transfer for Efficient GPU-NPU Phase-Disaggregated LLM Inference
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) inference exhibits distinct computational characteristics across its two phases: prefill is compute-intensive, whereas decode is more memory-bound. As a result, AI accelerators achieve varying levels of efficiency across the two phases. GPUs are well suited to prefill, but are often underutilized during decode. By contrast, NPUs can utilize their compute resources more effectively during decode. Motivated by this observation, we explore a heterogeneous architecture that integrates GPUs and NPUs, mapping prefill to GPUs and decode to NPUs to achieve high performance and efficiency. However, realizing such heterogeneous integration is challenging because LLM phase disaggregation requires KV cache transfer from prefill to decode (that is, from GPUs to NPUs), which is complicated by differences in inter-device communication mechanisms and KV cache tensor layouts. items.title: Trapping of nanofabricated SiO$_2$ high-aspect-ratio discs in an optical lattice
items.abstract: We describe the nanofabrication and loading of lithographically patterned, high aspect ratio $10$ $μ$m diameter silicon dioxide discs with thickness of $400$ nm into an optical standing wave trap in vacuum. We obtain motional spectra of the center of mass motion of the discs using a combination of interferometric and imaging methods. The method is capable of high-efficiency loading and optical trapping using small numbers of objects, of the order of a few particles, with customized geometries and sizes compatible with wafer scale nanofabrication methods. Disc-like particles in optical traps have been identified as promising candidates for detectors of high frequency gravitational waves or as sensitive accelerometers.

items.title: Hierarchical Fourier Phase Projection for Local Electronic Observables
items.abstract: In this letter, we develop hierarchical Fourier phase projection (HPP) for the calculation of local electronic observables. The method couples the spatial decay of the density matrix with a hierarchy of Fourier probes, improving accuracy through refinement, and making use of all previously evaluated responses. The variation in the calculated observables during the refinement process carries information on the residual error. We use a locality-based model to estimate the error from these changes with no extra probing calculations. In particular, we demonstrate the method for electron densities and nonlocal pseudopotential forces for fixed Kohn-Sham Hamiltonians of semiconductors, metals and thermally perturbed silica. The convergence is significantly accelerated by the spatial decay of the density matrix, especially if the density matrix is short-ranged. The number of probes necessary to...

items.title: Theoretical study of nitrogen-vacancy spin coherence enhanced by vacancy aggregation in diamond using cluster-correlation expansion
items.abstract: Annealing a semiconductor makes its vacancies mobile; they aggregate into multi-vacancy complexes that often carry spin. Such centres are a magnetic-noise source for any spin qubit among them, in silicon and silicon carbide as well as in diamond, and they are accordingly blamed for the decoherence of negatively charged nitrogen-vacancy (NV$^-$) centres in irradiated and implanted diamond, with two coherence records credited to removing them. Cluster-correlation-expansion simulations in which the spins outside each cluster keep exchanging spin projections in pairs reproduce the measured Hahn-echo coherence time of NV$^-$ centres in a substitutional-nitrogen bath to within 12%, inside the statistical uncertainty. items.title: Transport-Noise and Optical Witnesses of Electronic Multipartite Entanglement
items.abstract: Entanglement among particles distinguishes correlated quantum materials from conventional metals and semiconductors. Experimentally certifying intrinsic entanglement among interacting electrons in materials is important not only for classifying states of matter, but also for developing material-based quantum technologies. Here, we introduce a transport protocol for witnessing multipartite entanglement from the equilibrium current-noise spectrum, measured directly or reconstructed from optical conductivity. The appropriately integrated, symmetrized, and projected noise spectrum obeys an upper bound derived from microscopic model parameters. Unlike witnesses based on localized spins, our framework applies to general electronic states without requiring magnetic moments and remains invariant under single-particle basis transformations. items.title: Emergence of Bogoliubov Fermi Surfaces in hybrid Al/InAs heterostructures
items.abstract: We investigate the microwave electrodynamics of a proximitized two-dimensional electron gas in hybrid superconductor/semiconductor heterostructures. Using lumped-element resonators with inductor wires oriented relative to an in-plane magnetic field, we directly probe the superfluid stiffness via the kinetic inductance. As the field increases, the resonance frequency exhibits a non-monotonic and strongly anisotropic evolution that cannot be explained by orbital pair breaking alone. We show that this behavior is consistent with the emergence of Bogoliubov Fermi surfaces, which selectively suppress the supercurrent response depending on the direction of the magnetic field. Microscopic calculations of the stiffness tensor capture the observed anisotropy driven by the interplay of Zeeman and orbital Fulde-Ferrell effects. Our results establish microwave stiffness measurements as a sensitive p...

items.title: Bright and Dark Excitons in CrSBr: Local Ligand-Field Character and Band-Coherent Optical Selection Rules
items.abstract: Magnetic van der Waals semiconductors such as CrSBr host an intricate exciton landscape. Quasiparticle self-consistent GW theory with electron-hole ladder vertex corrections (QSGWc) has established the gap and the character of the bright XA (1.34 eV) and XB (1.8 eV) excitons. Why these bright excitons coexist, within a few tens of meV, with companions orders of magnitude darker has remained unexplained. Here we show that brightness is fixed by a symmetry of the structure: a mirror-glide exchanges the two Cr atoms of each layer, every exciton has a definite parity under it, and bright and dark partners are its even and odd members. The even sector carries the b-axis dipole; the odd sector is suppressed by about three orders of magnitude. items.title: Multi-stage Quantum Amplifier Readout Chain
items.abstract: Multi-stage cryogenic readout chains with a wide bandwidth and added noise within a few quanta of the quantum limit are frequently constructed using traveling-wave parametric amplifiers (TWPAs) as the first stage, and a semiconductor amplifier as the second stage. Unfortunately, for highly-scaled superconducting detector arrays, or quantum information systems, and space-based observatories, the power dissipation of the semiconductor amplifier becomes problematic from the perspective of available cryogenic cooling power near 3 K. Here we demonstrate a readout chain based on a two-stage kinetic inductance TWPA (KTWPA). This quantum-amplifier-based-readout-chain (QARC) provides sufficient gain that a cryogenic semiconductor follow-on amplifier can be eliminated without degradation of the system noise. items.title: Transmon Phase Gates Controlled by Superconducting Soliton DAC
items.abstract: We introduce a superconducting digital-to-analog converter (DAC) that filters control noise, provides native multiplexing, performs quantum gates in nanoseconds, and can be controlled by CMOS. This is achieved by transducing a trapezoidal drive pulse into a superconducting soliton, which is then held in the DAC load loop, applying flux to a mutually-coupled superconducting qubit or gate coupler. The analog flux output by the DAC can be easily controlled by varying the soliton hold time, or with a DC-biased tunable DAC-qubit coupler, allowing the DAC to perform a fixed-time, high-fidelity gate that's robust to fabrication variance or flux offsets in the quantum circuit. Our initial demonstration shows that the DAC can successfully perform 5.6 ns S-gates on transmons. items.title: Carruthers Data Processing Pipeline: Instrument Effect Correction
items.abstract: The Carruthers Geocorona Observatory -- launched in September 2025 -- is NASA's first mission devoted to investigating the fundamental nature of Earth's exosphere from its distant vantage in halo orbit around the Earth-Sun L1 Lagrange point. Its primary payload, the GeoCoronal Imager, consists of two coaligned photometric imagers that measure ultraviolet Lyman-alpha emission radiance from exospheric hydrogen simultaneously at wide- and narrow- fields of view. The imagers use MicroChannel Plate intensified Complementary Metal Oxide Semiconductor detectors, which are known to add various artifacts to the final image telemetered from the spacecraft, hereby known as instrument effects. items.title: Coexistence of Donor and Acceptor Hydrogen States in n-Type InN
items.abstract: Hydrogen often exhibits amphoteric behavior in semiconductors, but its role is in n-type InN remains unresolved. Wurtzite InN is a narrow-gap semiconductor with high electron mobility and is therefore attractive for high-speed electronics and optoelectronic applications. Here we use hard x-ray photoemission spectroscopy (HAXPES) to probe hydrogen-related electronic structure in as-grown and post-annealed InN thin films prepared at different grown temperatures. Post annealing, which reduces the concentration of hydrogen impurities in the films, shifts the core-level spectra toward lower binding energy, consistent with a chemical-potential shift associated with the passivation of electron carriers. items.title: Designing Strong and Broadband Nonreciprocal Thermal Radiation in Magnetic Topological Materials
items.abstract: Breaking reciprocity in thermal radiation opens opportunities for energy harvesting, sensing, and thermal management. Traditional nonreciprocal radiative semiconductor devices need external magnetic field. In this work, we predict a series of magnetic topological materials for magnetic-field-free nonreciprocal thermal radiation in the infrared regime, by combining first-principles calculations with Maxwell electrodynamics. We find strong and broadband nonreciprocity in magnetic Weyl semimetals (e.g., Co$_3$Sn$_2$S$_2$), outperforming the conventional semiconductor such as InAs. Furthermore, we propose universal material design recipes: strong nonreciprocity requires a large anomalous Hall response relative to the optical loss, whereas the broadband response favors large optical loss and small dielectric dispersion.
